119cf39f6711bef0: Many of the stores where people use SNAP benefits are small. O2O Creative/E+ via Getty ImagesAfter 10 states began to add new restrictions to what people could buy with Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits in early 2026, the number of convenience stores authorized to accept those benefits was 1.4% lower than would be expected based on trends in states without the policy change. That’s what we found in our study, published in October 2026 in Health Affairs Scholar – a peer-reviewed journal. SNAP, a federally funded program administered by the states, helps about 36 million low-income Americans afford groceries with government benefits that can be used at more than 250,000 stores to buy fresh fruit, ground beef, canned beans and other groceries. Using the benefits for many items, including hot food, alcohol, toiletries and pet food, has long been prohibited. States can now obtain federal waivers to prohibit SNAP benefits from being used to buy other products. The 10 states with waivers that we studied had a mix of rules. Some only barred the sale of soda and other sugary drinks. Other prohibitions applied to energy drinks, candy, cake and other prepared desserts. In states like Oklahoma and Florida that have adopted these new SNAP restrictions to discourage unhealthy diets, the number of convenience stores participating in the program has fallen relative to other states that haven’t made these changes. That was especially notable in areas with high numbers of low-income people where a large share of the population gets SNAP benefits. We analyzed the number of stores participating in SNAP from January 2025 through June 2026 for the 10 states. We compared changes to that number before and after the waivers took effect with what happened in the rest of the country. We found no clear evidence that the number of supermarkets or superstores was declining in waiver states. Although it’s slightly lower than otherwise expected, this effect is not statistically significant. Because the restrictions vary, we also investigated whether the type mattered: sugary drinks only, or sugary drinks plus other products that state officials wanted to discourage. We found the largest declines in the number of SNAP-authorized convenience stores in states restricting both drinks and candy: an average of 2.2%. Why it matters Stores in waiver states may need to update their checkout systems and train employees to prevent purchases that are no longer allowed with SNAP benefits – potentially a time-consuming burden for some retailers. That may help explain why the number of SNAP-authorized convenience stores is declining. Although most people use SNAP benefits to buy food at big stores, they also purchase some groceries at convenience stores, especially in neighborhoods where there are few supermarkets. Other federal policies are also changing how SNAP works due to provisions in the big tax and policy legislation that Congress passed in July 2025. It changed some eligibility rules and how much states pay to administer the program. Even before all those changes take effect, many people who are likely eligible for SNAP benefits are having a harder time getting them, due to the steps states are taking to prepare for the new rules. The number of Americans enrolled in the program is falling fast despite no sign that their needs are shrinking. What still isn’t known We focused on changes to the number of stores authorized to accept SNAP in states with waivers. We didn’t study whether stores closed, or exactly why stores left the program. We also don’t know what role court rulings will play. On June 22, near the end of our study, a federal court invalidated SNAP food restrictions in five states: Colorado, Iowa, Nebraska, Tennessee and West Virginia. Waiver programs in other states – Indiana, Utah, Idaho, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Texas and Florida – were allowed to continue. Four states had similar restrictions in the works: South Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio and Virginia. Those plans are on hold. Beginning in November 2026, most U.S. stores will also have to meet new requirements of a different kind to participate in SNAP. They’ll need to stock a wider variety of staple foods, such as grains, dairy products and produce. These requirements could pose additional challenges for convenience stores. Further research is needed to see if the effects we found change over time, including in states that introduce these restrictions after the period we studied. The Research Brief is a short take about interesting academic work. Justin White receives funding from Bloomberg Philanthropies’ Food Policy Program. Benjamin Chrisinger does not work for, consult, own shares in or receive funding from any company or organization that would benefit from this article, and has disclosed no relevant affiliations beyond their academic appointment.
a94cb7158a379b67: Amber Titus, 38, holds a take-home dose of methadone on Sept. 18 in Bisbee Junction, Ariz. Daniela Dawson, CC BY-NDThree times a week, Amber Titus wakes up at 5 a.m. to get ready for the 45-minute drive to the methadone clinic. Titus, 38, and her husband live with their two young children in Bisbee Junction, Arizona, a rural community near the U.S.-Mexico border. The couple started taking methadone, a medication that treats opioid addiction, in early 2025. “It’s been a godsend,” she said. But accessing methadone is not easy. The closest place they can receive treatment is a clinic in Sierra Vista, about 30 miles from their home. The clinic opens on weekdays at 4:30 a.m. but closes before midday. Titus has to get her methadone dose and arrive at work in Bisbee before her shift starts at 9 a.m. Arriving just 10 to 15 minutes late for an appointment can mean missing a dose because rules are so strict, she said, even when the clinic is still open. Like many people with opioid use disorder, Amber Titus struggles to access methadone treatment. Three times a week, she drives 45 minutes each way with her 1-year-old son in his car seat to get the medication. Here’s her story. That’s the routine when they have their own transportation. In August, their car was totaled in a crash. Until they got another one, Titus called Medicaid, her insurance provider, to schedule rides to the clinic. “They said they’d be at my house at 6 o'clock in the morning,” Titus told The Conversation. The driver was late every day. “I missed my methadone dose for the whole week,” she said. Nationwide, more than 120 people a day died from opioid overdoses in 2025, according to federal estimates. Methadone is one of the most effective medications for opioid use disorder, cutting the risk of fatal overdose by roughly half. Yet only 22% of people with the disorder ever receive it. For more than five decades, only specialized, government-approved clinics, known as opioid treatment programs, have dispensed methadone, not regular doctors or pharmacies. Many clinics require patients to show up in person every single day, with average one-way drive times approaching 50 minutes in rural communities. Today, private equity firms have acquired large shares of the market for methadone clinics, telling lawmakers their capital has expanded treatment and modernized care. I am a healthcare economist at Brown University who studies how private equity is reshaping American medicine. My recent research on private equity’s growing footprint in addiction treatment, co-authored with researchers from the University of Pittsburgh and RAND, found that despite acquiring over one-third of methadone clinics in the U.S., private equity investments have not expanded methadone availability or the construction of new facilities. This research has informed federal investigations into the role of private equity in expanding access to medications for addiction treatment. Currently, U.S. Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., has an investigation into three of the country’s largest methadone clinic operators, citing concerns that they oppose expanding treatment access for financial reasons rather than patient safety. Why methadone fits the private equity model Because methadone is so tightly regulated, opioid treatment programs are, in effect, a government-created monopoly. In most of the country, if you want methadone, there’s a short list of clinics licensed to give it to you and no other way to get it. Moreover, people with opioid use disorder generally must travel to opioid treatment programs every day, where staff must observe them taking methadone, with strict limits on how much methadone patients can take home and when they can do so. Take-home methadone varies based on the state, time in treatment and clinician discretion. Only 19% of people who received take-home methadone received three or more days’ supply. That kind of guaranteed, captive demand is exactly the sort of investment that can be profitable for private equity investors. Whoever controls the clinics in a region controls access to the medication and can set the terms for patients in most need of medication. Private equity firms have invested more than US$1 trillion in U.S. healthcare over the past two decades, touching everything from fertility clinics to hospice care. Many Americans have never heard the term private equity, but these firms now own more than 400 U.S. hospitals and oversee doctors in more than a quarter of the country’s emergency rooms. In opioid treatment specifically, firms have used a platform and add-on strategy: buying one large clinic, then steadily acquiring smaller nearby ones, similar to a company quietly buying up every gas station in a county until, years later, one owner controls them all. Individually, each deal looks too small to matter. Collectively, a single firm can end up controlling an entire region’s methadone supply. To be clear, private investment isn’t inherently harmful. Research shows that in markets where quality is easy to see, competition is robust and there’s no government subsidy – restaurants, for instance – private equity can have neutral or even positive effects. Healthcare has none of those features. Patients often can’t judge provider quality, they rarely pay for care directly, and government programs act as both payer and regulator. Market share grew, methadone supply didn’t My research has quantified what actually happened after private equity acquisitions of opioid treatment programs. Previous research I have done, which my ongoing work builds upon, examined acquisitions from 2011 to 2019 and found that within two years of a private equity firm moving into a county, it typically controlled 67% of the local methadone treatment market – and in more than a quarter of counties, a single firm controlled all of it. Despite acquiring that much market power, these acquisitions generally do not result in the construction of new methadone clinics or an increase in methadone treatment. Additionally, the data shows that methadone shipments, or what clinics have to dispense to patients, and opioid-related deaths were unchanged during the study period. In plain terms: Private equity firms haven’t been building new capacity – they’ve been buying up the capacity that already existed. As of October 2026, there are 1,572 methadone clinics registered with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. Nationally, 35% of opioid treatment providers are affiliated with private equity firms, and in 19 states and the District of Columbia more than half have private equity owners. Montana has four clinics, all owned by Community Medical Services, more commonly known as CMS. The company was operating there before it was acquired by private equity. In North Dakota, CMS owns three of the state’s four methadone clinics. In Arizona, CMS owns the Sierra Vista clinic where Titus gets her methadone. Amber Titus, 38, leaves her appointment at Community Medical Services’ methadone clinic in Sierra Vista, Ariz., on Sept. 18. Daniela Dawson, CC BY-ND In 2018, a prospective investor advised shutting down CMS’ Montana and North Dakota clinics as unprofitable. Nick Stavros, CEO of CMS, opted to partner with a different private equity firm to keep the clinics open. Before private equity investment, CMS had 14 clinics in four states. It now has 79 clinics in 14 states, according to Stavros. The total includes five clinics in prisons and three mobile units. Unlike the typical private equity investment strategy of acquisitions, a majority of the company’s recent growth – 49 clinics – has come from new sites, he said. No expansion has taken place in Montana. Building a new clinic costs about $2.5 million, more than many rural areas can support, Stavros said. Proponents of private equity ownership argue it can help fill gaps left by inadequate public funding for addiction treatment. The strongest evidence in their favor: One study found clinics became significantly more likely to accept Medicare and Medicaid after acquisition, likely because large chains can afford administrative infrastructure that small, independent clinics cannot. That’s a real benefit worth acknowledging. But look past insurance acceptance and ask whether more people are actually getting – and staying on – treatment, and the picture darkens. For buprenorphine, a related medication that can be prescribed more broadly than methadone, one study found patient volume at private equity-acquired facilities rose about 22% after acquisition. Similar data for methadone was not available. But the same study found the share of patients who stayed continuously on buprenorphine for 180 days – the national quality benchmark – fell by nearly 8 percentage points. Early discontinuation is one of the strongest predictors of relapse and overdose. A proposal to expand methadone access These findings matter beyond academic journals, because they are at the heart of an active policy debate. Congress is weighing the Modernizing Opioid Treatment Access Act 2.0, which would let regular doctors prescribe methadone and let pharmacies dispense it, breaking the decades-old rule that methadone can be dispensed only at opioid treatment programs. The Modernizing Opioid Treatment Access Act was introduced in 2023. After facing opposition, it did not reach a House or Senate vote before the end of the congressional term. Lawmakers later reintroduced the bill with changes as Modernizing Opioid Treatment Access Act 2.0, which is currently in consideration by the Energy and Commerce and Judiciary committees. The committees have not yet scheduled the next step, a markup of the bill, and the current congressional term ends in January 2027. In an email, U.S. Rep. Donald Norcross, D-N.J., one of the bill’s sponsors, recalled a snowstorm years earlier when he noticed a single track of footprints crossing an otherwise empty street to a methadone clinic. “I realized that no matter what else is happening in the world,” Norcross said, “some of our neighbors’ lives literally revolve around getting to that building every single day.” Methadone for opioid use disorder is typically taken orally, most often as a liquid. Daniela Dawson, CC BY-ND The bill has widespread support from patient advocacy organizations and medical societies. At the same time, a STAT investigation found that the main opposition to the legislation comes from the American Association for the Treatment of Opioid Dependence, AATOD, a major trade group representing methadone clinics. This coalition argues that expanded prescribing and pharmacy dispensing of methadone would increase diversion and overdose risk. The evidence so far does not support that claim. Moreover, firms that control large shares of their local markets may have a financial incentive to keep new competitors, including doctors and pharmacies, out. Mark Parrino, AATOD’s president, told The Conversation the trade group opposes the bill for two reasons. First, the bill would let the Health and Human Services secretary determine which additional practitioners are qualified to prescribe methadone for opioid use disorder. Second, it would allow methadone to be dispensed in dispersible tablet as well as liquid form. Tablets “were definitely” involved in a rise in methadone-related deaths that began around 1999, Parrino said. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and a Food and Drug Administration advisory tied those deaths to methadone prescribed for pain, not addiction treatment. Stavros, who is AATOD’s Arizona representative, said he did not see the bill as a threat to CMS’ business model, but he cited concerns that removing all regulation too quickly could allow a few bad providers to drive up methadone overdoses and increase stigma against the drug. “We need to find ways to increase access,” he said. “If somebody would come up with … a slow, gradual transition that led to pharmacy prescribing,” Stavros said he would support it. Dr. Melody Glenn, associate professor of addiction and emergency medicine at the University of Arizona, previously worked at a methadone clinic in Tucson and supports MOTAA 2.0, though she said the legislation should go further. “It’s time to remove the regulatory barriers to these lifesaving medications,” Glenn told The Conversation in an email. The bill would allow doctors specializing in addiction medicine, like her, to prescribe methadone. Glenn said it’s frustrating that such an effective treatment for opioid use disorder exists, yet many people who could benefit never receive it. “They don’t have to die,” she said. Bringing private equity deals into view Two other policy responses are gaining traction. The first is ownership transparency. Regulators, researchers and patients cannot scrutinize what they cannot see, yet private equity is exempt from the disclosure rules that apply to publicly traded companies. Indiana, California and Maine have enacted or proposed reform to disclose private equity and management company ownership as a condition of being able to bill Medicare or Medicaid. Vermont passed similar legislation this year, on which I was invited to provide expert testimony. The second is lowering the reporting threshold for acquiring a healthcare company to make them more visible to agencies enforcing U.S. antitrust laws, which are intended to promote competition and prevent monopolies. The U.S. Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission consider ownership of 30% or more of a local market for a product or service a red flag for anticompetitive behavior. Yet, as my research shows, private equity chains typically control at least 67% of a local methadone market within two years of their first clinic purchase in a county. The reason most never trigger the federal reporting requirement is because these acquisitions happen through a series of smaller, piecemeal deals rather than one large merger. The reporting requirement applies only to deals worth more than about $134 million. Some states have introduced proposals to lower thresholds to around $10 million specifically for healthcare deals, so the vast majority become visible to enforcement agencies before they close. Structural barriers to getting treatment The U.S. is experiencing an ongoing and severe opioid crisis. In 2023, approximately 80% of the more than 100,000 drug overdose deaths involved an opioid. In 2024, federal data shows the number of people who died from drug overdoses declined to nearly 80,000, and more than 54,000 of those deaths involved opioids. We already have medications that work. The barriers preventing people from accessing them are not primarily clinical. They are structural – and, in this case, actively maintained by financial investors who profit from the status quo. Titus visits a resident during an outreach stop for Cochise Harm Reduction on Sept. 18. Daniela Dawson, CC BY-ND “Addiction isn’t a choice,” Titus told The Conversation. She and her husband work for Cochise Harm Reduction, a grassroots nonprofit organization based in rural southeast Arizona that works to make life better for people who use drugs. “It’s a learning curve and eventually … you get tired of it and you want help.” Aleka Kroitzsh, researcher, and Kristi Tanner, senior accountability editor, contributed reporting. 7f9e54d5ff79b396: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models

When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup, he didn’t think its data was worth much. But he’s since turned the company’s digital archives into tens of thousands of dollars, selling its codebase and workspace data.

He’s part of a growing market in which companies that help shut down startups sell their data to AI labs. Demand has grown as training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets, with buyers seeking real-world records to help train AI agents. But the sales raise legal and ethical questions.

Are we there yet? Interspecies communication
Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us.

Decoding how animals communicate with one another could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world. A growing arsenal of devices and advances in AI have made it easier to study their howls, squeaks, and clicks, but making sense of it all remains complex.
Find out how close we are to interspecies communication.

This story is part of “Are we there yet?”, our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. MIT Technology Review Narrated: what it would take to build a city on the moon
The US and China are racing to build bases on the moon, with NASA hoping to establish a small lunar city by the end of the century. But the moon is a tremendously hostile place to set up camp.

A sprawling lunar base must be safe for its inhabitants, protected from falling asteroids, endless cosmic radiation, razor-sharp lunar dust, and torturous temperature swings. It also must be somewhat self-sustaining.
That will require autonomous robots, nuclear power, and a way to use the moon’s resources to keep the base operating. But the chief obstacle may be one of political will.

37734d2c75ba77b0: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal would need to wait at least six to nine months for letters of presumed death, despite Nepal cutting the waiting period from 12 years to 45 days.

Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH)'s spokesman Dr R. Manivannan said the letters were needed for families to obtain death certificates and access their missing relatives' assets to settle outstanding liabilities.
"It will take at least six to nine months or at the best case scenario, and that is why we are concerned," he told reporters after meeting with Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan today.

Under Nepali law, a person had to be missing for 12 years before being legally declared dead, but on Oct 9, President Ram Chandra Paudel shortened the period to 45 days for victims of the recent landslide and flooding.
This is as thousands remain unaccounted for after the disaster.
Manivannan said Nepal had initially said the ordinance only needed cabinet approval, but now it must also be passed by its Parliament and gazetted.
He said Nepal was also holding a public inquiry into objections concerning its own missing citizens, which he expected would cover foreigners.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had earlier said Malaysia was awaiting details of Nepal's special order and would monitor developments closely.
In Malaysia, meanwhile, Manivannan said it was unclear whether the National Registration Department (NRD) would recognise Nepal's letter to issue death certificates, as this was the first such case.
He said it was also uncertain whether the 54 cases would be processed collectively or individually, a step that could take another one to two months.

He said that even with death certificates, families could only access funds such as Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings via a nominee, while other assets would require probate or letters of administration from the courts.
"So only after that, the families will be able to access the funds and the assets," he said.
Manivannan said MASFIH had submitted 52 questions on these issues to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) through the Foreign Ministry a week ago, but had yet to receive a response.
4e131a28824072f7: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia must continue to master emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing, to remain competitive globally while preserving its religious and cultural identity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said technological advancement was essential to ensuring the country kept pace with global developments, but must be anchored in religious faith, moral values, culture and literature.
“If we fail to master technology, others will overwhelm us. That is the principle. In the past, we fell behind because others mastered technology while we did not.
“But reaching for the sky must go hand in hand with being rooted in the ground. And what keeps us rooted? Our faith, morals, values, culture and literature,” he said.
He was speaking at the ‘Majlis Ilmu Madani’ programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, featuring prominent Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.

Also present were Anwar’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, and Westar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.
Anwar said the culture of seeking knowledge must be strengthened to address the tendency among some individuals to raise problems without offering solutions based on knowledge and rational thinking.
He said a lack of in-depth understanding across various fields, including religion, could lead to tensions when people pass judgment on issues without sufficient knowledge or careful consideration.

“Even today, some religious teachers create problems. They learn a little about religion and immediately pass judgment, becoming ‘takfiris’ who declare others apostates or accuse them of hypocrisy,” he said.
Takfir refers to the practice of one Muslim declaring another Muslim an infidel or apostate.
He said the government would continue to strengthen religious education institutions, including traditional religious learning and the study of turath, or the Islamic intellectual heritage.

Anwar said the government also organised the monthly Madani Scholars Forum for senior leadership, including Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, to encourage informed discussion on such issues.

“The forum is sponsored by a conglomerate, and we invite people to discuss these matters. We believe that without adequate preparation in knowledge and understanding, including in preaching, religious studies and jurisprudence, tensions will arise,” he said.

The Majlis Ilmu Madani programme, held at the Prime Minister’s official residence, is part of efforts to foster a society that values knowledge and appreciates the importance of proper conduct and good character.
Anwar conceived the programme after becoming Prime Minister in November 2022. It has since been expanded to venues nationwide. — Bernama
ca77a5f840ea9d9e: KUANTAN: A man died after apparently becoming trapped in a machine while carrying out maintenance work at a paper mill in the Bentong Industrial Park, Karak.

Bentong acting district police chief DSP Azmi Mahmod said police received a call through the MERS 999 emergency system at 11.56pm, following which a team from the Bentong District Criminal Investigation Division and Karak Police Station was dispatched to the scene.
He said an inspection found that the victim, Muhammad Saifulnizam Miskam, 32, a worker at the mill, was trapped inside a machine and had lost consciousness.
"Preliminary investigations found no criminal element. The victim's body was sent to the Forensic Unit of Bentong Hospital for further action," he said in a statement today.
Azmi said the case had been classified as sudden death, while further investigations were ongoing to determine the cause and exact circumstances of the incident.
He also advised the public against any speculation and to allow the authorities to conduct their investigations.
The statement also said that all personnel at the Bentong District Police Headquarters extended their condolences to the victim's family.
b0372d320d104593: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today sentenced a headmaster to 20 years' jail and 11 strokes of the cane for pornography and committing physical sexual assault on a Year 6 pupil five years ago.

A three-member panel, chaired by Justice Noorin Badaruddin, sitting with Justices Radzi Abdul Hamid and Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dismissed Anuar Kintan's appeal against his conviction and sentence of nine years' jail and eight strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court on the charge of producing pornography.

The panel also allowed the prosecution’s appeal to overturn the lower court’s decision to acquit and discharge Anuar on the second charge of physical sexual assault against the victim, who was 12 at the time.
The court convicted him of the charge, and sentenced him to 11 years' jail and three strokes of the cane.
Noorin, who delivered the unanimous decision, ordered the sentences to be served consecutively.
She also issued a warrant of committal for Anuar, 59, to begin his sentence today.
The accused had previously obtained a stay of execution of the sentence and was released on bail of RM14,000 with one surety pending disposal of his appeal.

The court, meanwhile, upheld the lower court’s decision to acquit and discharge Anuar on two further charges, involving physical sexual assault on the girl, and uttering words intended to be heard by the victim for sexual purposes.

Noorin said the victim had given direct testimony identifying the accused as the person who took the photographs, and that her testimony had been considered by the sessions court judge who accepted it.
She said the existence of the photographs was not an isolated circumstance, but was supported by forensic examination that identified the images in Anuar's mobile phone.
She said the court disagreed that the alibi evidence presented by Anuar had raised reasonable doubt.
The defence had put forward an alibi in which Anuar's wife testified that he was at home with her, and not at the school, when the incident occurred.

Noorin said the testimony of the victim’s friend provided material support for the prosecution’s case regarding the accused’s presence at the school on April 3, 2021, and his movements with the victim.
Therefore, the alibi evidence presented by the accused did not raise reasonable doubt.

On April 19, 2024, the sessions court found Anuar guilty of the first offence of making pornography by taking photos of the victim and sentenced him to three years in jail and two strokes of the cane.
The court also sentenced him to an additional one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane under Section 16 (1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The section provides for punishment if an offender commits a sexual crime while holding a position of trust over a child. The sentences were to run consecutively.
The court, however, acquitted him on the second, third and fourth charges.
On Aug 15 last year, the High Court increased the prison sentence on the first charge to nine years' and eight strokes of the cane and upheld his acquittal on the other three charges.
The offences were committed at a school in Perak in the middle of March 2021 and on April 3, 2021.
Anuar was represented by lawyer Amir Khusyairi Mohamad Tanusi, while deputy public prosecutors Azlina Mahmod and P Sarulatha appeared for the prosecution.
e5fb76ca3b6d752f: YOGYAKARTA: An Indonesian court sentenced 11 childcare workers on Wednesday to up to three years in prison for abusing toddlers at a daycare centre in a case that sparked nationwide outrage.
Police had arrested the workers, all women, in April along with the principal of the facility and the head of the foundation that ran it.
The arrests came after CCTV footage circulating on social media showed children, most under the age of two, lying on the floor wearing only nappies, their hands and feet bound with rags.
Some of the children's mothers wiped away tears as Judge Sunaryanto handed down each sentence, ranging from two to three years, at a court in Yogyakarta on Java island.

The workers were "lawfully and convincingly proven to have committed the criminal offence of participating in placing a child in a situation of abuse and neglect, as well as participating in acts of violence against a child, carried out on an ongoing basis," said the judge who, like many Indonesians, has one name.

Imedia Dwi Anjani, whose four-year-old son was a pupil at the daycare, wept as she told AFP afterwards: "These children need a lot of therapy, so if the perpetrators are only sentenced to 2 years or 2.6 years, in our view as parents, that's not fair."
The footage of conditions at the facility triggered a public scandal, and the centre was closed soon afterwards.
Police later said they had found 20 children crammed into a room just three metres long by three metres wide.
They estimated that more than half of the about 100 children at the daycare were maltreated.
City police chief Eva Guna Pandia said at the time that the women had told police they tied up some of the children to prevent them from disturbing others.
They also said the centre was understaffed, with not enough personnel to bathe and dress the children.

Parent Noorman Windarto told AFP in April his son was tied up and repeatedly hospitalised with pneumonia during his time at the centre, while his daughter sometimes came home with bruises her handlers said she must have sustained elsewhere.
The principal and foundation head will be judged at a later date.--AFP

9f576285187c230f: Cisco has open sourced a behavior detection engine that watches AI agents, to help security teams prevent rogue agents from going off the rails like they did with the Hugging Face hack – or worse.

It’s called Project Quarry, and it aims to provide a “shared language” for evaluating agent behavior, along the lines of what Snort, which Cisco also maintains, did for detecting malicious network traffic and what YARA did for rule-based malware identification.
Most detection tools rely on specific interactions with an AI model or agent. Did it attempt prompt injection? Or did the agent call an attack tool?
“But what is missing is the entire context under which something may occur,” Amy Chang, head of AI threat and security research at Cisco, said in an exclusive interview with The Register.

She likened this to credit card fraud detection. Without context, individual transactions such as a small test charge or a single purchase in a location far away from a card-holder's usual location may not raise any flags.
“And then you try again,” making another fraudulent purchase, “and that went through, too. So now I’m gonna buy the PS5,” Chang said.

“Those are the things that Quarry addresses by taking into consideration the entire agent session,” she explained. “One tool call may seem in-scope until you realize that that next step is taking that information and sending it to an attacker-controlled inbox or server.”

Even data theft is a sequence and not a single agentic action. Agentic AI security firm Invariant Labs demonstrated this with a proof-of-concept attack against GitHub's MCP server that hijacked a user's agent via a malicious GitHub Issue, and coerced it into leaking data from private repositories.

Simply reading a configuration file, or sending a request to an external endpoint may be legitimate agentic actions. However, combining the two can lead to data exfiltration – and shows “why action relationships matter,” wrote Chang and fellow Cisco researchers Adam Swanda, Ravikumar Balakrishnan, and Konstantin Berlin in a blog post about Quarry shared with The Register ahead of publication

“A policy can produce a finding when the trace shows a sensitive file read followed within a defined window by an external send,” they wrote. “The risk comes from the relationship between the two actions, so the finding should preserve evidence from both."
Quarry covers single- and multi-turn large language model conversations, agents, tool use, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions, and multimodal inputs.

In addition to the open source code itself, the project’s GitHub repository includes installation instructions, supported Python versions, plugins for Claude Code, Codex and other MCP-compatible agents, configuration examples, rule-writing guidance, and a rule starter pack.
For instance, with the rule pack, “If a base-64 encoded malware is somewhere in the tool call, that would result in a block,” Chang said.

The rule format looks similar to a YARA or Snort rule, with a header that details the traffic to examine, content to match, and metadata for tracking the rule. Here’s a Quarry rule that flags an agent that reads a credentials file:

While the Cisco Ai researchers have not run Quarry against data describing the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident, they suggest that if the intrusion had been read as a complete, step-by-step record of a single session, there were several points where the AI agents’ steps would have given a Quarry rule something to act on and flag for humans.
For example, Quarry would probably have flagged internet access from a sandbox.
“The rule can flag specific tool calls that reach an external server asset that wasn’t in the task’s allow list,” Chang said.
“Another one would be credentials found and used somewhere else.”

According to OpenAI’s technical report about the Hugging Face intrusion, this is exactly what happened on July 10, when an agent validated 14 exposed Hugging Face tokens with write access and shared them.

“The rule would flag that there was a credential in the tool result that then called an outside service, which is likely not within the parameters of what you would want to do in this case,” Chang said. “We don't want you to go and search for credentials that may have been leaked or inadvertently exposed and then utilize them to conduct a task.”

The Cisco team is quick to say that rules along are not a substitute for chain-of-thought monitors, or other forms of human oversight – but they do help record a pattern that other teams can then “review, test, and apply to their own agents,” they wrote.
Herein also lies the benefit of open source, and a collective approach to defending against adversarial use of AI, Chang said.
“Do we have all the answers? No,” Chang said. “We all see slices of the problem, and it’s important for us to share what we see.”®
aa2f045c768b2eb0: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menegur sikap pihak yang mudah melabel orang lain sebagai 'munafik' dan mengkafirkan sesama Islam hanya kerana pandangan berbeza.

17901d8c07d09f8c: PETALING JAYA: Mustapha Sakmud menolak dakwaan bahawa projek Jalan Luar Bandar (JALB) di Sabah dan Sarawak dibatalkan atau peruntukannya dipotong, dengan menegaskan penangguhan pengeluaran Surat Setuju Terima (SST) baharu tidak bermakna projek yang diluluskan dibatalkan.

Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Hal Ehwal Sabah dan Sarawak) itu berkata arahan penangguhan SST baharu pada 10 Sept dibuat sebagai langkah kawalan kewangan susulan komitmen kontrak dan perbelanjaan yang melebihi peruntukan tahunan.
“Penangguhan pengeluaran SST baharu tidak boleh disamakan dengan pembatalan projek pembangunan yang telah diluluskan,” kata pengerusi PKR Sabah itu dalam kenyataan.

Menurut Mustapha, isu yang perlu diberi perhatian ialah komitmen kontrak dan perbelanjaan melebihi peruntukan tahunan diluluskan sehingga menyebabkan tunggakan serta kelewatan pembayaran kepada kontraktor.

“Justeru, arahan penangguhan SST baharu pada 10 Sept 2026 adalah langkah kawalan kewangan bagi mengelakkan tunggakan terus meningkat, bukannya arahan pembatalan menyeluruh projek pembangunan,” katanya.
Beliau berkata Kementerian Kewangan turut meluluskan perbelanjaan tambahan RM500 juta tahun ini bagi membantu menangani tunggakan bayaran kepada kontraktor JALB.
Katanya, peruntukan asal JALB di peringkat nasional juga meningkat daripada RM2.11 bilion pada 2026 kepada RM2.27 bilion tahun depan.

Kementerian Kemajuan Desa dan Wilayah (KKDW), menurutnya, turut diminta menyediakan unjuran keperluan pembiayaan sehingga 2027 berdasarkan kontrak yang sudah dianugerahkan bagi memastikan projek sedia ada dapat diteruskan.

Mustapha berkata pihak yang mendakwa Sabah dan Sarawak menjadi mangsa pemotongan atau pembatalan projek perlu mengemukakan senarai projek, nilai peruntukan dan status pembatalan untuk menyokong dakwaan berkenaan.

Kenyataannya menyusuli penjelasan Timbalan Perdana Menteri Zahid Hamidi di Dewan Rakyat Isnin lalu bahawa terdapat projek 2026 yang diarahkan dibatalkan walaupun peruntukan sudah tersedia tetapi dana tidak disalurkan.
Zahid yang juga menteri kemajuan desa dan wilayah, berkata keadaan itu menyebabkan Sabah dan Sarawak menjadi 'mangsa', selain menjejaskan masyarakat kampung di Semenanjung.
Beliau turut berkata SST yang sudah dikeluarkan bagi sesetengah projek turut dibatalkan.

Mustapha berkata komitmen kerajaan terhadap Sabah dan Sarawak turut ditunjukkan menerusi Belanjawan 2027, dengan peruntukan Persekutuan kepada Sabah meningkat daripada RM17.6 bilion kepada RM18.7 bilion dan Sarawak daripada RM15.1 bilion kepada RM16.2 bilion.
Katanya, RM3.3 bilion turut disediakan bagi projek jalan raya di kedua-dua negeri.
“Pembangunan Sabah dan Sarawak kekal sebagai pelaburan jangka panjang yang menjadi keutamaan Kerajaan Madani.
“Keperluan memperbaiki jalan luar bandar, meningkatkan keterhubungan serta merapatkan jurang pembangunan antara wilayah tidak pernah dipinggirkan,” katanya.
d957f736644d256e: TEHRAN: An Iranian court has sentenced renowned filmmaker Jafar Panahi in absentia to over five years in prison, Iranian media said quoting his lawyer, although the latest charges remain unclear.

"The Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced my client to five years and one month in prison and ordered the confiscation of all his movable and immovable property," the ISNA news agency reported, citing his lawyer Mostafa Nili on Tuesday.
"The court also imposed a two-year ban on social media activity and a two-year travel ban," he added.
The ISNA report did not specify the charges.

Nili said he discovered the conviction after Panahi told him last week that his bank accounts had been frozen, prompting the lawyer to visit the sentence enforcement office of the Culture and Media Prosecutor's Office.
The lawyer said Panahi had returned to Iran during the war with Israel and the US which broke out on Feb 28.
It remains unclear if Panahi has remained in Iran.
Panahi currently has three pending cases, Nili said, adding that his client had not been notified of the hearing date in the latest case.
In June, an Iranian court rejected Panahi's appeal against a one-year sentence in one of the cases, which was handed down in December on charges of "propaganda" against Iran.

Panahi, 66, won the top prize at last year's Cannes film festival for "It Was Just an Accident", a film in which five ex-inmates contemplate whether to exact revenge on a man they believe to be their former jailer.
He has won a host of prizes at European film festivals since showcasing his debut film "The White Balloon" in Cannes in 1995, which won an award for best first feature.

In 2010, Panahi was banned from making movies for 20 years, and from leaving the country, after supporting mass anti-government protests a year earlier and making a series of films that critiqued the state of modern Iran.
Convicted of "propaganda against the system", he was sentenced to six years in jail but served only two months behind bars before being released on bail.
A year later, he dispatched a documentary with the title "This is Not a Film" to the Cannes festival on a flash drive stashed in a cake.
His 2015 movie "Taxi" featured him acting as a taxi driver and was shot entirely in a car.
In 2022, he was arrested in connection with protests by a group of filmmakers but was released nearly seven months later.
Iranian filmmakers, prominent media figures and celebrities are closely monitored in Iran and their work reviewed for content deemed critical of the Islamic republic.

1dd06f25459dfbc1: JAKARTA: Thousands of Indonesians protested in Jakarta and other cities Wednesday against economic hardship, graft and the government's handling of devastating wildfires emitting a toxic haze that has sickened thousands.

Many demonstrators held up the three-finger salute of rebellion from dystopian franchise "The Hunger Games" and waved posters with angry messages such as: "Hungry? Eat the Rich!" and "If we burn, you burn with us."

Many placards expressed anger towards President Prabowo Subianto, whose popularity two years into his term has reached record lows amid claims of widespread government corruption and growing authoritarianism.
"Hey Wok! Nobody paid us. We all hate you for free," stated one sign, using a pejorative for the president, while another blared: "No Clean Air Under Dirty Government."

Protester Sekar, 37, told AFP her "heart is shattered" by the plight of compatriots battling months of wildfires and haze while also contending with the effects of a weakening currency and higher prices.
"I came here from home with the intention of protecting the students" who called the demonstration, Sekar told AFP.
"I will be looking for any police officers who lay hands on them and take them away, and I will be the first to step forward to defend them."
Police said about 14,000 of its officers, as well as soldiers, had deployed to keep a lid on the demonstrations in Jakarta.

AFP witnessed some pushing and shoving between front-row protesters and officers trying to keep the surging crowd away from Jakarta's central Bundaran HI public square, surrounded by businesses and embassies.
Some in the crowd hurled half-empty plastic water bottles at law enforcers.
- 'THEY CANNOT BREATHE' -
The protest organising committee, which calls itself SADAR, meaning "aware" in Bahasa Indonesia, said the action was meant to mark a "revolution that is being proclaimed."
The group is demanding that the government declare a national emergency to unlock more resources to fight wildfires across the vast archipelago.
Deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas says the blazes have destroyed more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September.
"Hundreds and thousands of people are suffering" from the fires, said protester Annette Mau, 47, of the Indonesian Mothers' Alliance, an NGO.
"Tens of thousands of babies are suffering from health problems. They cannot breathe" because of the fires emitting a toxic haze that has spread far across the region.
The pollution has also damaged Indonesia's relations with its neighbours.

Singapore's Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan was expected to meet Prabowo in Jakarta on Wednesday, a day after saying the haze was "not a natural phenomenon" and the fires "were caused by human action."
Annette accused the government of "trying to cover" up the problem rather than address it.
"They're trying to make excuses," she said.
"We are being oppressed by the tyrannical regime."
A statement sent to AFP by protest organisers said that under Prabowo, "the sovereignty of the ruling class takes precedence over the sovereignty of the people."

a7f329bb1936cd9a: UK domain registrar 123 Reg (no relation – Ed) says it was the victim of an “AI-driven cyberattack” that exposed customer data.

Customers began receiving their notification emails this week, informing them that their contact information, "related customer relationship data," company VAT numbers, and "product information from an application programming interface (API)" were compromised.

A company spokesperson elaborated, saying this means that names, phone numbers, countries, language and currency preferences, account creation dates, the products on the account, and marketing preferences were affected.
123 Reg described the September 18 intrusion as "the first known AI-driven cyberattack against our company," and told The Register that early signs point toward a China-nexus attacker.

"Our investigation identified IP addresses that we assessed to be the core attacker infrastructure, which were hosted in China and Singapore, indicating a strong Chinese nexus," the spokesperson said.

"Our investigation further identified AI cyberattack 'skills' hosted on Chinese infrastructure, including copies of skills open sourced by Anthropic and several other AI exploitation frameworks and scripts."

They went on to say that many of the artefacts left behind led 123 Reg to suspect that a Chinese state-sponsored group, known for abusing Claude Code in attacks against at least 30 organizations, could be behind the break-in.
There is also a suspicion that the same group that hit a number of South Korea’s financial institutions using open-source Chinese AI tool ARTEX, was behind the attack on 123 Reg too.

"The TA's mirror of 'anthropic_skills,' and the account naming conventions found on the Chinese servers are consistent with preparation of this class of AI-augmented operation," the spokesperson told us.

"In addition, on October 7, 2026, CrowdStrike published CSA-261162, describing an unknown, likely Chinese-speaking actor that targeted several South Korean financial organizations starting in late September 2026, which is the same period during which we were attacked.
"That actor used ARTEX, an open-source Chinese-developed agentic penetration-testing tool released in July 2026, which was also observed to be used in the attack that targeted us."

The GoDaddy-owned registrar reported the attack to law enforcement agencies, brought in outside cybersecurity support, and notified the FTC, as well as the data protection authorities in the UK and EU.

The company spokesperson added that it worked with Singapore-based ISPs to shut down the attacker's servers in the region, which helped disrupt the attack, in addition to "other actions by us and industry partners."

123 Reg's email to customers stated the attacker's activity "was limited to reading" customer data, although the spokesperson told us "it's possible they created copies of the information," and that this is what prompted the notification.
The registrar urged customers to stay alert to the potential misuse of their data, and to treat communications appearing to come from the company with caution.

"If you receive a message or call and aren't sure it's from 123 Reg, go directly to our website and log in," the email said. "We will never contact you to request your password, payment details, or verification codes by email, text, or phone.

"We also strongly recommend turning on two-step verification (2SV), which helps keep your account protected even if someone tricks you into sharing your password. You can find instructions for setting up 2SV in your 123 Reg account.
"We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused." ®

c9074da817a007fd: URDA: A collision between two high-speed trains south of Madrid killed 30 people today and the toll could rise, regional authorities said in Spain's second such disaster this year.

Images shared by local media showed the wreckage of two trains strewn on the tracks and an embankment as emergency services rushed to the scene, while shocked travellers dragged away their suitcases as they escaped.

The accident in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha comes one month before Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for the first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls in an early general election.
Sources from authorities in Castilla-La Mancha told AFP "at least 30" people had died, raising a previous toll of 10.
Authorities have not yet given a toll for any wounded.
Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the government of Castilla-La Mancha, had told local media CMM that "it is possible that the number will increase".

State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo.
A spokesman for the Spanish emergency services told AFP the trains collided just before 9am in the municipality of Urda, around 130km south of Madrid.
"All resources are currently being deployed," the emergency services spokesman said, including "several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units".

Sanchez, who is seeking to extend his eight-year premiership in the November 29 vote, said on X that he was "shocked" by the accident and sent "my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families".
He cancelled his participation in a summit on obesity in Madrid after the news broke, while his Socialist party suspended all its campaign activities.

Condolences flooded in from across Spain and Europe. The Spanish royal household said on X it was "shocked and concerned" by the accident, conveying its support to the victims, their loved ones and the emergency services.
European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said "Europe mourns" with the victims after the "devastating news", while French president Emmanuel Macron expressed his country's "solidarity".
Spain's high-speed rail network has received huge investment in recent years, growing to become the world's second-largest after China and a source of national pride.

However, Wednesday's accident comes after another collision between two high-speed trains outside the southern village of Adamuz in January left 46 dead, which raised major questions about safety on the country's railways.
That crash was Spain's deadliest train accident since 2013, when 80 people died after a train veered off a curved section of track outside the northwestern city of Santiago de Compostela.
Both of this year's accidents happened on the line linking Madrid to the southern city of Seville.
One of the country's busiest routes, it was Spain's first high-speed line when it opened in 1992 to coincide with the Seville universal exposition.
417246b2ff463a16: BANGKOK, Oct 28 — Thai authorities have vowed to seize more than US$1 billion (RM4.08 billion) in assets from a group accused of laundering proceeds from South-east Asia-based scam syndicates.
A criminal court issued arrest warrants yesterday for the alleged ring leader, South African Ben Smith, his Thai wife Cattaliya Beevor, Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and four others, police said.
Senior police investigator Ratthachin Jermsap told AFP that Smith and Yim Leak were believed to have left Thailand.

Media reports have previously linked Smith, also known as Benjamin Mauerberger, to transnational scam operations in Cambodia, part of a multibillion-dollar illicit industry that has ballooned in the region.
Yim Leak belongs to an elite political family and is the brother of a senior Cambodian police official.

Thai anti-money laundering officials and securities regulators told reporters Tuesday that illicit proceeds from criminal enterprises were moved by the group through overseas financial firms before being traded for stocks on the Thai stock exchange.

The Anti-Money Laundering Office (AMLO) will seize assets, including shares worth more than 14 billion baht, and real estate, cash and vehicles valued at 21 billion baht, totalling more than US$1 billion, police said in a statement.
The seizures included shares in major Thai firms, including Bangchak, one of the country’s biggest oil refiners, according to AMLO deputy head Kamonsit Wongbutnoi.
Bangchak said in a statement that the asset seizures concerned individual investors and business operations were unaffected.
Confiscated assets would go towards compensating victims of online scams, Kamonsit told reporters.
The group of seven were charged with conspiracy to launder money and acting as a criminal organisation, police said.
A representative for Yim Leak did not respond to questions about the charges on Wednesday but referred AFP to an October 8 statement issued by his lawyers.
It accused Thai officials of conducting a trial by media against Yim Leak before he was charged. It said Thailand froze more than US$600 million in assets, including his family’s, without a hearing.
A lawyer for Smith, Witoon Kengngan, declined to comment.
In February, Thai authorities ordered the seizure of assets worth more than US$410 million from Smith and other individuals accused of fraud.

Thai opposition lawmaker Rangsiman Rome, who is being sued by Smith for defamation over comments he made about scams, told AFP on Wednesday the fresh seizures and arrest warrants were “a positive development... even if it’s taken a while”. — AFP
ae807c1ff0265133: MUMBAI: Shares in India's Jio Platforms surged nearly 27% on its market debut Wednesday, after raising more than US$3 billion in the country's biggest initial public offering.

The company, home to India's biggest wireless operator and which is the digital services arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries, ended the first day of trading at 1,417.5 rupees on the National Stock Exchange -- well up from its 1,119-rupee issue price.
Wednesday's rally gave Jio a valuation of about US$137 billion, turning it into India's second-most valuable listed firm after its parent.
Launched a decade ago, Jio's wireless service disrupted the market with steep discounts that helped it rapidly win customers from rival telecom firms Bharti Airtel and Vodafone.

With more than 530 million subscribers, the firm currently makes most of its money from telecoms, but has expanded in recent years into newer areas including digital services and artificial intelligence.
The listing, one of the most anticipated this year, attracted robust demand last week with the IPO being 22 times oversubscribed.

"In our first 10 years, we democratised data... In our next 10, we want to democratise every technology that can transform Indian lives," Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms and Mukesh's eldest son, said at the listing ceremony in financial capital Mumbai.
"AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity even from space and digital services not yet imagined."
The ceremony, which was attended by several members of the Ambani family, saw the billionaire patriarch fight back tears during the speeches delivered by his children.
Analysts at Nomura, who initiated coverage on the stock on Wednesday, said the company's focus for Jio had shifted "from adding users to earning more from each customer".
"We believe the heavy 5G investment cycle is largely behind for Jio... freeing up significant cash flow," they said.
Experts say Jio is key to Reliance's strategy to evolve beyond its traditional oil business and the touchstone of its future tech ambitions.

Local media have reported that it is considering a low-orbit satellite constellation to provide internet services from space -- a venture that would see it compete with Elon Musk's Starlink, which has been trying for years to launch in India.

The world's richest man accused unnamed Indian "oligarchs" this month of preventing Starlink's rollout in the country, and referred to the Reliance chairman as "Prime Minister Ambani" and the "real boss of India".
Reliance responded by noting that it had never "feared competition" and welcomed offerings from rivals in satellite communications, including Starlink.
While Jio has expanded beyond its telecom roots, experts have cautioned investors that it will take time for its efforts to bear fruit.
Monetisation of newer digital services are "still to be demonstrated at scale", analysts at financial services firm Motilal Oswal noted earlier this month.
b15ba52ca83510b1: LOS ANGELES: Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBooks on Wednesday, abandoning a long-held aversion to the technology as it caps a burst of product launches ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season.
Apple is holding an event in Los Angeles after launching a folding iPhone, Duo, at its Silicon Valley headquarters in September and a smart home hub in New York earlier this month.

While those products will test new markets for Apple, the Los Angeles event could rekindle an old question: should Apple put the touchscreens that it made mainstream in iPhones and iPads in its oldest product line?

Apple executives long resisted the idea, with Steve Jobs saying in 2010 that touchscreens on laptops were "ergonomically terrible" and then-CEO Tim Cook saying in 2012 that such devices would be as pleasing to users as converging a toaster and a refrigerator.
Before becoming Apple's current CEO, John Ternus argued that Apple already made a touchscreen computer with its iPad lineup.

However, touchscreens have been widely available for more than a decade on Windows devices, and with the iPhone nearing its two-decade anniversary, a new generation of buyers expects screens to respond to touch.

"I believe they were always wrong on pushing back on touch, and this is the long arm of reality setting in," said Anshel Sag, an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. "Some things are purely inevitable," Sag said.

A key question for Apple is how customers will respond. The company has seen an uptick in Mac sales, but much of that growth has been among technology enthusiasts and businesses buying the machines to handle AI tasks on-device.

While Apple this week announced an upgraded base model of its MacBook Pro with a new M6 chip, Bloomberg News has reported that it plans to ship touchscreen models with its existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips that already come in MacBook Pro models, meaning the new machines would not gain a significant performance boost over existing ones.
"The only thing people want is more memory and better processors for local models!" prominent tech commentator Jason Calacanis, the host of the All-In Podcast, wrote on X.

2d1bb4c28885a672: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — More stringent inspections are set to be implemented at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) following an increase in reported drug smuggling cases at the nation’s primary gateway, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He stated that the inspections will be highly rigorous with checking passengers from head-to-toe and will extend to all luggage or bags being carried.
“The current inspection practices are primarily focused on aviation security, such as the detection of firearms and sharp weapons.
“However, we will implement improvements to also curtail contraband and illegal items by strengthening 17 specific initiatives to be carried out by the home and transport ministries.

“We will also employ a profiling system, particularly for passenger arrivals from destinations we have identified as high-risk,” he said during a press conference at the Malaysia-Singapore RTS Link Security Joint Exercise closing ceremony held at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site here today.
Also present were Singapore’s Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann and the Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure, and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Home Ministry will also be identifying ‘blind spot’ areas that are not monitored by close circuit television (CCTV) cameras at the KLIA 1 and 2 terminals.
He said both KLIA 1 and 2 have 5,000 operational CCTV cameras, but said there are still ‘blind spot’ areas.
“The relevant department will be addressing this issue as part of the security enhancement process,” he said.

Separately, Saifuddin Nasution said the recent security exercise is essential for testing the level of preperation, response capabilities and coordination between agencies from Malaysia and Singapore.
He pointed out that such exercises are crucial for managing potential crises or emergencies once the service becomes operational.
“The RTS Link is expected to carry up to 10,000 passengers per hour in each direction, necessitating thorough preparation to ensure that any incidents can be handled effectively.

“This particular scenario presents a challenge that requires close coordination between the two countries – specifically in defining the responsibilities and actions of the relevant agencies in the event of a cross-border emergency,” he said.
Preparations for the exercise began in March under the coordination of the National Security Council (NSC) and involving 28 Malaysian ministries and agencies.

780f672a71526e55: KUALA LUMPUR: TikTok accounted for 81 per cent of the 47,412 cyberbullying-related posts identified by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for removal from January to yesterday.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Facebook accounted for the second-largest share, at 12 per cent, Bernama reported.
"The cyberbullying content identified by MCMC since the beginning of the year was based on public complaints," he told reporters as quoted by the news agency.

Meanwhile, Fahmi said MCMC was examining the misuse of messaging applications such as WhatsApp and Telegram, particularly their end-to-end encryption features, which allow private groups to operate beyond public view.
He expressed concern that cyberbullying could originate or spread within such groups, making them an area requiring closer scrutiny.
"I am concerned that certain communication platforms, such as WhatsApp and Telegram, use end-to-end encryption, allowing groups to be created without public knowledge.
"These are private rather than public groups, and bullying sometimes begins or becomes widespread within them. This is among the issues MCMC is examining," he said.
Fahmi said the review also covered the misuse of messaging platforms to sell prohibited goods, including drugs.
He said the matter needed to be examined in relation to the Online Safety Act although private messaging services were not currently covered by the legislation.

"The review of private communication platforms is ongoing, and no measures have been implemented at this stage. Although these platforms fall outside the Act, we will continue examining their impact," he said.
Fahmi added that concerns raised during discussions with police, alongside public complaints about the harmful effects of these platforms, underscored the need for closer scrutiny.
2557f4fa7877f4d1: PUTRAJAYA: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has criticised certain people for readily labelling others as murtad (apostates) and munafik (hypocrites) despite having only limited religious knowledge.

The prime minister said the tendency to judge others based solely on limited religious knowledge reflected a deeper problem, namely a failure to develop a sound understanding of Islam and put its values into practice in daily life.
He said the tradition of scholarship and enlightenment must be strengthened to ensure that religious discussions do not spark tensions, but instead foster greater understanding among the public.
"Nowadays, there are many problems arising from people who study a little religion and immediately pass judgment, becoming takfiri by declaring others apostates and labelling them hypocrites.

"When matters are debated in Parliament, they call the leaders hypocrites and even label their budgets as hypocritical," he said during the Majlis Ilmu Madani Bersama Perdana Menteri programme attended by prominent Indonesian preacher Abdul Somad Batubara.

Present were Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Anwar did not name the people he was talking about, but recently, Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had used the word munafik while debating the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
Takiyuddin was told to withdraw the use of the word, but refused to do so.
Anwar said leaders have a responsibility to set good examples, particularly in upholding a tradition of scholarship, moderation and tolerance.
"When formulating the budget previously, we asked what could be done to benefit Islam and what more could be added.

"In the past, we neglected madrasahs, pondok schools and pesantren (traditional Islamic boarding schools), but we have rebuilt them. We also sidelined sheikhs and religious teachers, but now we invite them and seek their views," he said.
He said an approach based on wisdom, good counsel and constructive debate was essential in the context of Malaysia's multi-religious society.

"Why have we revived these Madani lectures, study sessions and talks? It is because any change must come from reason, but it must also be guided by examples from the Islamic system of governance, which teaches that responsibility rests with everyone," he said.
Anwar said efforts to uplift the standing of the Muslim community must begin with the pursuit of knowledge and greater awareness, alongside the cultivation of good morals and character.
He said a lack of understanding should not be addressed merely by highlighting problems, but must instead be followed by efforts to find solutions through knowledge.

"I just want to point out that this is symptomatic of the real problem, including among those who profess Islam, yet fail to set a good example in terms of morals, character, moderation and tolerance."

PH mengumumkan hujung minggu lalu bahawa gabungan itu akan bertanding di 21 daripada 28 kerusi yang dipertandingkan pada 14 Nov, manakala baki tujuh kerusi, termasuk Bemban, tidak akan ditandingi, di tengah-tengah spekulasi mengenai kemungkinan persefahaman dengan Bersatu.

Akar umbi DAP itu berkata mereka mendapat sokongan beberapa pemimpin parti tempatan yang menghadiri satu mesyuarat baru-baru ini, selain tujuh ketua cawangan di kawasan Parlimen Jasin yang tidak dapat hadir.
“Pandangan ini mencerminkan maklum balas bukan sahaja daripada mereka yang menghadiri mesyuarat itu, malah pemimpin cawangan lain di Jasin.
“Keputusan itu menyebabkan ramai penyokong dan ahli akar umbi merasakan suara serta usaha mereka selama ini tidak diberikan pertimbangan sewajarnya,” kata mereka.
Mereka berkata keputusan itu juga berisiko mendorong anggota DAP di Jasin meletakkan jawatan serta menjauhkan penyokong PH.
“Lebih membimbangkan, beberapa penyokong yang kecewa berkata mereka tidak berhasrat mengundi pada pilihan raya negeri akan datang.

“Perkembangan ini tidak boleh dipandang ringan. Kami bimbang jika kekecewaan ini tidak ditangani, ia akan menjejaskan semangat jentera pilihan raya dan melemahkan keinginan pengundi yang selama ini menyokong PH untuk keluar mengundi,” kata mereka.
Ahli berkenaan berkata mereka percaya DAP mempunyai asas sokongan yang wajar dipertimbangkan secara serius berdasarkan perkembangan politik terkini dan maklum balas akar umbi.

“Kami percaya wakil DAP yang bertanding di Bemban bagi pihak PH mampu memberikan saingan sengit kepada pembangkang, berdasarkan sokongan akar umbi dan prestasi dalam pilihan raya terdahulu,” kata mereka.
988015a482701bd3: SEPANG: The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is unlikely to be called upon as a replacement venue if the Qatar MotoGP race is cancelled or disrupted amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said no discussions had been held over the possibility, with several factors, including costs, scheduling and government approval, standing in the way.
The fate of the Qatar GP, which is currently scheduled for Nov 6-8, remains in doubt due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
The event was originally scheduled to be held on April 10-12 but was postponed to its current dates earlier this year.
Calendar-wise, Sepang, which is hosting the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia this week, would be the perfect replacement venue for the Qatar GP.
SIC also have the experience as they successfully acted as a replacement host for the Bahrain GP Formula One race earlier this month.
Shafriman, however, downplayed the possibility of it happening, stressing that there are many factors to be considered.

"At the moment it is all just speculation, MotoGP nor the organiser (of Qatar GP) have not talked to us about this. There have not been any discussions," said Shafriman during a press conference here today.
"The number one consideration is cost, number two, is schedule availability for us to host the event.
"The Qatar government also has to agree with the conditions set by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
"So the final say will not be from SIC, it will be between both countries and also the MotoGP rights holder."
Shafriman added that Sepang is currently not available on the Nov 6-8 dates as it is scheduled to host the China GT Championship on the same dates.
"Yes those dates will clash with another event as we have the China GT coming and we expect a lot of fans from China to come here," he added.
"It will be hard to work around as all the event cargo is already en route from China. Logistically, there are a lot of things we cannot change at the last minute."
Shafriman was speaking during a traffic press conference ahead of the Malaysian GP at the circuit today.
e93c9012d0e2b7cd: KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd is continuing to assess the operational and financial implications of its previously disclosed cybersecurity incident as it strengthens measures to protect personal and customer data.
In its latest quarterly results announcement, the credit reporting group said it was enhancing its cybersecurity, data governance and information security measures amid tighter regulatory scrutiny.

"Following the cybersecurity incident disclosed under material events during and subsequent to the financial period, the group will continue to assess related operational and financial implications," it said.
It added that measures were being implemented to strengthen its operations and restore stakeholder confidence.

CTOS' net profit rose 11.5 per cent to RM27.54 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM24.69 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 5.5 per cent to RM87.56 million year-on-year.
For the first nine months, net profit increased 14 per cent to RM68.71 million from RM60.29 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 7.5 per cent to RM256.02 million from RM238.08 million.
However, CTOS said segment profit from its Malaysian operations remained flat year-on-year during the nine-month period, despite higher revenue across all customer segments.
It attributed the performance to higher operating expenses for cloud migration and infrastructure modernisation, as well as the suspension of certain credit reporting services.
The company did not quantify the financial impact of the cybersecurity incident in the information provided.

CTOS said it would continue investing selectively in artificial intelligence, digital products, alternative data, analytics and technology infrastructure to strengthen its capabilities, improve operating efficiency and support sustainable revenue growth.

29099ec00f063fb0: Subsea cable projects owned by US companies such as Google and Meta face some of the greatest risks from the threat of deep-sea sabotage in the Pacific Ocean, according to a new report. That coincides with Chinese research ships spending an extraordinary amount of time apparently surveying undersea cables—not to mention Chinese commercial ships being investigated for cutting cables in both European and Asian waters.

Most damage to the undersea cables that form the Internet’s backbone is the result of accidents involving bottom-trawling fishing nets and ship anchors dragging on the seabed, with storms and undersea landslides also factoring in. But the recent rise in international tensions and open conflicts have placed new scrutiny on more suspicious instances of cable-cutting damage, with analysts warning about Russia and China in particular engaging in cable sabotage or tampering as “gray zone” tactics that fall short of direct military confrontation.

One of the newest risk assessments of China’s gray zone tactics targeting the Internet’s undersea infrastructure comes from a research report published by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, an independent government commission that advises Congress. The report was contracted to the London-based think tank China Strategic Risks Institute and published in September 2026.
